reason: The hypothesis directly restates the well-known finding from P8 and P33 that increasing Al content in CoCrFeNiMnX alloys transforms the oxide from non-protective Mn-oxides to protective Al2O3, and extends this to Si and Mn as comparative X elements. The mechanism invoking Pilling-Bedworth ratios is taken from P43, and the role of microstructure is a generic idea from P11 and P14. The proposed comparison of Al, Si, and Mn in a single- vs. multiphase state is a minor extension of the Al-content studies already reported, without combining findings from different papers into a new proposal or resolving a conflict.
copied_elements: Varying X (Al, Si, Mn) in CrFeCoNiX
Al or Si forms protective Al2O3 or SiO2
Pilling-Bedworth ratio governs stress and adhesion
Single-phase vs. multiphase effect on diffusion paths
Predicted outcome: Al/Si alloys form thin, adherent scales; Mn alloys form thick, spalling scales
